question: Should GitHub-backed sync be allowed to rename existing over-limit display names to a capped fallback, or should existing GitHub-backed rows be grandfathered like hosted rows?
rationale: This is a stored catalog compatibility and product-policy choice; automation should not decide whether existing source-backed skill names may change on upgrade.

options.title: Grandfather GitHub-backed names
options.body: Preserve existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names for matched rows unless the source explicitly changes under an approved policy, then add a regression test for that upgrade path.

options.title: Approve rename-on-sync
options.body: Accept the compatibility risk intentionally, document that existing GitHub-backed names may be capped on the next sync, and require upgrade proof for that behavior.

options.title: Pause until policy is set
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers define the display-name maximum and legacy handling across hosted and GitHub-backed sources.

recommendation.title: Grandfather GitHub-backed names
recommendation.body: Preserve existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names for matched rows unless the source explicitly changes under an approved policy, then add a regression test for that upgrade path.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick owns the recent central publish and GitHub-source sync code where the compatibility choice lands.
